doc.title: Quincy Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Why America needs a secretary of the arts: music is God's work
summary: Baker asks how to get the US to lead on the arts. Jones repeats his call for a secretary of the arts, says American music already rules the world, and that music is God's work unlike the military.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: I wonder, what is it going to take to ultimately move the United States to take a lead role in some of this stuff? Because basically, the first thing that gets cut is anything that has to do with the arts.

You know I know that. That’s why I’m being a pain in the butt, and I don’t care, about secretary of the arts, secretary of the arts, secretary of the arts. We need – what is wrong with us? Why does it take us so long. It’s time for us to have a – we have a culture. We don’t have to prove that. We have to get in there and act like we own it and stand behind it. It’s there. It’s going to go without you. It’s already gone. It’s not like something you have to establish or maybe American music will be influential in the rest of the world. Are you crazy? It’s the king of the music in the world.
How does that ever get to a public? We’ve got people who are ignorant or people who don’t give a damn or people who threaten.
And thinking militarily – what the hell is that? It means nothing. That doesn’t have power. That’s not God’s work.
But the music is God’s work. You can’t see it, smell it, touch it, taste it, but you can feel it.

You called it. The power of music. You’ve watched it in Venezuela the difference it made with those kids all of a sudden. I don’t know if you’ve ever seen the video. They run it on “60 Minutes” a couple of times.
